title: Call Back Before Five
brief: No-Overtime Milk Tea launches at 8 tomorrow morning. Franchisees are chasing the posters, but Ah-Kai has put the print files on hold at Lanshan Plaza.

lines.text: Hold off on sending the print files. I got to the last page and couldn't trace the pattern on the cup sleeve in the AI image.
The franchise group chat's already announced an 8 AM launch. The client even asked if they could reuse the image for next month's store opening.
The quote just says 'new product promotion.' It doesn't say where we can use AI or whether franchisees can print the artwork.
The client just messaged me. She's worried her boss will think she's holding things up. The printer needs files by five. Give her something she can take back to him.
I'll call. Can you ask Wei how many placements he can cover tonight with the photos we shot?
On it. Ask the client this, too. If she can only have one thing by morning, does she want the in-store poster or the order page?

steps.prompt: You owe the client a call before five. What can you agree to deliver?

options.text: Pull the AI image and rebuild the whole set tonight with product photos. Keep the launch on schedule and send the coupons a day later.
options.feedback: You're up with the designers past midnight. The opening crews get matching photo posters, and the brand's website gets the new look too. The coupons go out a day later, so the launch misses its planned push to drive orders.
options.insight: The yearbook notes that Coca-Cola's Masterpiece animation took eight weeks to make. Without AI, it could have taken five times as long.

options.text: Tell the client you can't trace the image, get written approval to use only product photos, and deliver the order page first thing tomorrow.
options.feedback: The client uses your confirmation email to brief her boss. She agrees to open orders on time and wait two days for the franchise posters. You and Ah-Kai spell out where AI is allowed and what franchisees can use, then send the contract addendum for sign-off.
options.insight: The yearbook flags three things for account executives to discuss with clients: where AI can be used, what the contract requires them to disclose, and who owns the rights.

options.text: Agree by phone to use the AI image on the order page to start taking orders. Hold the franchise print files until you've checked the source.
options.feedback: Orders start coming in at eight. Before noon, a franchisee has printed a screenshot as a table sign, and a customer posts asking whether it's a collaboration with another brand. The client calls to ask how it ended up in print, and you have to ring each store to get it taken down.
options.insight: The yearbook points out that AI makes content cheaper to produce and slower to verify. A check that once took a second might now take a minute, ten minutes, or even an hour.
